answer: Each agent identity must periodically complete a unique computational proof bound to its own key — a puzzle no two identities can share or parallelize. An attacker spawning thousands of fake identities pays the full compute cost for each, so expense scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Earned reputation then acts as a mirror: peers check that claimed history matches observable behavior, and a walnut-hard shell of locked stake opens only after sustained honest service, letting an agent wander the network freely only after proving it is real.
